function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

**Reykjavík – the clear winner** | Why Reykjavík stands out | What you’ll find | |---------------------------|------------------| | **Largest & busiest ice‑hockey scene** – Home to *HK Fram* (the country’s oldest club) and the national team’s training base. | • Two full‑size rinks (Laugardalshöll & Tjörnin Ice Arena).
• Regular domestic matches, international friendlies, and occasional NHL alumni exhibitions. | | **Convenient access** – Keflavík International Airport sits just outside the capital, so getting to the arenas takes minutes. | • Public transport links (buses, taxis, rideshare apps). | | **Everything else you’d expect from a capital** – Museums, cafés, bars, shopping districts, and vibrant nightlife. | • Hallgrímskirkja church, Harpa concert hall, Perlan museum, Old Harbour area. | | **Fan culture & community** – Friendly locals who love their sport, often welcoming visitors into locker rooms after games. | • Meet‑ups organized through fan clubs, social media groups, and sometimes free “fan nights.” | --- ### Other good options if you’re willing to venture off‑capital | City | Highlights | |------|------------| | **Akureyri** | • Known as the “Capital of North Iceland”.
• Hosts *ÍBV*’s home games at the small yet cozy *Álftaneshús* arena.
• Great scenery—close to waterfalls, hot springs, and whale‑watching tours. | | **Hveragerði** | • Small town with a decent indoor rink (*Vaðra í Hveragerðinum*) where regional leagues play.
• Famous geothermal spa nearby (Geysir Hot Springs). | | **Kópavogur / Hafnarfjörður** | • Suburban towns near Reykjavík with secondary rinks and youth programs. Good for family trips. | --- #### Quick tip for planning your trip: 1. **Check the schedule:** Domestic fixtures run mostly Saturday–Sunday evenings. Use the official *Icelandic Hockey Association* website or the *Úrvalsdeildkarla* app for dates/times. 2. **Book tickets early:** Popular match days sell fast, especially when the national team plays abroad or during playoffs. 3. **Combine sports with sightseeing:** After a game, stroll around downtown Reykjavík, grab a bowl of traditional Icelandic fish soup (“plokkfiskur”), then head back to the rink for a nightcap at one of the many craft beer pubs. Enjoy the chill vibes—and remember, even if you don’t catch all the action live, watching a game in front of enthusiastic crowds is part of the Icelandic experience!
